items.note: Page (last updated 3 Dec 2025) says the ZFE applies inside the périphérique from 1 Jan 2025 and a Crit'Air sticker is needed. Only unclassified vehicles (<1% of the fleet) are banned, on weekdays 7-9h/16-19h, excluding public holidays. Parking on the street stays allowed during restriction hours. It lists 12 named P+R sites reachable from outside. Title matches.

Page published 13 Feb 2024 (updated 6 May 2025) describes a PROJECT and a planned schedule in future tense ('Le déploiement des piétonnisations sera progressif: fin 2024... mars 2025... juin 2025'; ZTL extension 'prévue'). It does not confirm that any phase was completed. The figures check out: 8 ha to 84 ha, ZTL +900 m to 1.9 km, only authorised vehicles including residents'. The automatic bollards are mentioned as part of a planned 2 M EUR budget and a photo caption about pedestrian zones. The page does not say the ZTL 'is controlled by' bollards. Date 2025-06 is the planned last phase, not a confirmed event.
items.corrected_text: Nantes Métropole's plan, confirmed after a 2023 consultation, is to extend the central pedestrian area by 8 hectares to 84 hectares. It is to be phased in from late 2024 (quai de Versailles south, Hôtel de ville south), through March 2025 (Joffre and a new limited-traffic zone), to June 2025 (Cathédrale south). The limited-traffic zone, where only authorised vehicles including residents' may drive, was to grow by 900 m to 1.9 km.

items.note: The 24matins article is dated 25 Oct 2022 and is forward-looking. It says the 14 Oct 2022 council approved phased paid parking from spring 2023 and that 'tarification solidaire' for residents would apply 'dès le 1er avril prochain'. It cannot confirm the scheme actually started on 1 April 2023. The 30-90% reduction applies to the first permit; standard 180 EUR/year is stated (example: 126 EUR instead of 180). It is a single secondary news source.
items.corrected_text: According to a news article from October 2022, Nantes city council approved income-based ('solidarity') pricing for residents' on-street parking permits, due to start on 1 April 2023. It gives reductions of 30-90% on the first permit, against a standard price of 180 euros a year.

items.note: Page (last updated 20 Oct 2025): 62 P+R, 8,500 car spaces of which 4,957 with access control. 20 controlled sites run by Nantes Gestion Équipement; the others are free, run by Nantes Métropole, without barriers. Occasional users pay 4.50 EUR for parking plus one return trip for up to 5 people. Mobilités/LiberTan card holders with a transit subscription park free up to 24h. Title matches.
Page says: since April 2021, public transport (excluding the airport shuttle) is free on Saturdays and Sundays, and P+R sites are too when combined with the transit network. Title matches.

Page (published 15 Apr 2024) announces fares applying from 1 July 2024: formule illimitée 539 EUR/yr instead of 525, monthly 62 instead of 60, 10-ticket pack 17.50 instead of 17. Single ticket unchanged at 1.80 EUR. Title matches.

Page was published 9 June 2023 (updated Aug 2025) and is an ANNOUNCEMENT in future tense. It says that from mid-September 2023 the Tan, Nge parkings, bicloo and Effia offers 'seront réunies' under Naolib, and that naolib.fr 'indiquera en temps réel' P+R availability. It does not confirm either happened. Names and date intent are correct.
items.corrected_text: In June 2023 it was announced that from mid-September 2023 the Tan public transport, Bicloo bike-share, NGE parkings and Effia offers would be grouped under one name, Naolib. A naolib.fr website was to show real-time availability at park-and-ride sites.

items.note: BOAMP PDF 24-15703 (sent 8 Feb 2024) is a concession award notice from Nantes Métropole: DSP for the 'Centre-Ouest' car parks Aristide Briand, Descartes, Cité internationale des congrès, les Machines, Médiathèque and les Nefs. Value of contracts awarded: 21,434,007 EUR. 'Au moins un lauréat a été choisi'. Data transmission for dynamic signage and the parking observatory is listed. No winner is named, and the text correctly says so. The only issue: 1 Jan 2024 to 31 Dec 2028 is given as 'Durée estimée' (estimated duration), not a fixed term.
items.corrected_text: Nantes Métropole awarded a concession to run the 'Centre-Ouest' public car parks (Aristide Briand, Descartes, Cité internationale des congrès, Les Machines, Médiathèque and Les Nefs). The estimated term is 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2028 and the value about 21.4 million euros. The operator must also supply data for dynamic signage and the metropolis's parking observatory; the award notice does not name the winning operator.

items.note: CRC Pays de la Loire page dated 27.03.2025 covers 2018-2023. It says: more than 11,000 spaces operated; 'baisse de la fréquentation comme pour l'ensemble des parkings publics de la métropole'; some city-centre car parks are ageing despite major works. Title matches.

Same CRC page says NGE has handled the 'contrôle du stationnement payant sur voirie, par lecture automatisée des plaques d'immatriculation (LAPI)' 'depuis la rentrée 2024'. 'Rentrée' means early September, not October/autumn. The page does not mention vehicles.
items.corrected_text: According to the regional audit chamber, since the start of the 2024 school year (September 2024) NGE has carried out enforcement of paid on-street parking using automatic number-plate reading (LAPI).

items.note: Page (published 17 Apr 2025): e-Totem signed an agreement with Nantes Métropole in April 2024. It is called an operator and a French company that makes its own charge points. 1,250 charge points are to be installed progressively in the 24 communes by 2026, in addition to 234 already in city-centre multi-storey car parks and several P+R. Title matches.

Page (published 12 Nov 2025) confirms: P+R Babinière entered service on 12 Nov 2025 with 450 car spaces (28 with EV charging) and 103 bike spaces (55 new + 48 existing). Access is by Mobilités/Libertan card with a subscription, or a 4.50 EUR P+R ticket. It does NOT say the site is on the 'extended tram line 1'; that link appears only on a different page (item 12).
items.corrected_text: The Babinière park-and-ride in La Chapelle-sur-Erdre, with a tram link to Nantes station, opened on 12 November 2025. It has 450 car spaces, 28 of them with EV charging, and 103 bike spaces. Entry needs a transit pass or a 4.50-euro park-and-ride ticket.

items.note: Page (published 10 Mar 2025): Bas-Chantenay opened in January (219 car spaces) and Estuaire in early March 2025 (119 car spaces), both with access control (barrier). Title matches.

Page published 20 May 2026 (updated 3 June 2026). It says that from 3 June the renewed Naolib app 'va rassembler' transit and parking services: multi-storey, P+R and on-street in Nantes and Rezé. Features are parking availability, booking a space on the fly, and online subscriptions. What is due early 2027 is 'services vélo (location longue durée et information)', i.e. long-term bike rental, NOT bike-share. Launch is stated as scheduled, not reported as done.
items.corrected_text: A renewed Naolib app was set to replace the previous one from 3 June 2026. Alongside transit, it brings in multi-storey car parks, park-and-ride and on-street parking in Nantes and Rezé, with parking availability, space booking and online subscriptions. Long-term bike rental and bike information are due to be added in early 2027.

items.note: The URL serves Semitan's 'Rapport d'activités 2024' (PDF created 3 June 2025), NOT a 2025 report. The figure 158.7 million does not appear anywhere in it. Its headline under 'La fréquentation 2024' is 154.1 million trips, and the text says ridership grew 5.5% on 2023 and passed the 2019 level. The 148.6 million figure comes from a chart whose year labels are scrambled in extraction, so it is dropped. On paper tickets, the report only says that in 2025 Semitan would roll out new ticketing to progressively replace them with contactless tickets (a plan, not a completed retirement).
items.corrected_text: Semitan's 2024 activity report gives 154.1 million trips on the Nantes network in 2024, 5.5% more than in 2023 and above the 2019 level. It says that in 2025 Semitan planned to roll out new ticketing to progressively replace paper tickets with contactless ones.

items.note: Page (published 1 July 2026) on the EMC² 2025 survey (fieldwork Sept 2024-Mar 2025). For Nantes Métropole: solo car 43% (2015) to 38% (2025), cycling 3% to 7%, public transport stable at 15%. 'Published in July 2026' refers to this article's date. Title matches.
Page (published 19 Sept 2024): 852,919 visits across all VAN sites, 6 July-8 September 2024, +4% vs 2023. Foreign visitors were 30% over the summer (château and Machines data). Title matches.

corrected_summary: In 2023 Nantes Métropole announced that its transit, bike-share and car-park services would be grouped under the Naolib name, and a renewed Naolib app combining transit with multi-storey, park-and-ride and on-street parking was set to launch on 3 June 2026. A regional audit report published in March 2025 said attendance at NGE's car parks was falling, as at all public car parks in the metropolis. A low-emission zone has applied inside the ring road since January 2025, and new park-and-ride sites opened in 2025. Semitan reported 154.1 million transit trips in 2024, and the 2025 mobility survey found solo car use in Nantes Métropole fell from 43% of trips in 2015 to 38% in 2025.
